content: I'll read the test image first to analyze the symptoms.

The test image shows tomato plants with severe, sudden whole-plant wilting while leaves remain mostly green — a classic vascular wilt symptom. Plants are collapsed/drooping dramatically while neighboring plants appear healthy. This pattern strongly suggests a bacterial wilt disease.

Key visual features:
- Whole-plant collapse with green leaves (not yellowing)
- Sudden wilting pattern
- Commercial field setting with black plastic mulch
- Surrounding plants appear healthy

Top candidates: Bacterial_Wilt, Southern_Bacterial_Wilt, Verticillium_Wilt

Let me view one reference image for Bacterial_Wilt.

The reference image for Bacterial_Wilt shows the classic diagnostic test — a stem cross-section in water with bacterial ooze streaming down, confirming vascular infection and bacterial streaming. This corresponds well to the field symptoms in the test image.

**Analysis:**
- The test image shows dramatic, sudden whole-plant wilting of tomato plants with leaves remaining green — hallmark of bacterial vascular wilt
- Adjacent plants appear completely healthy, suggesting soil-borne focal infection
- The rapid collapse without yellowing/browning rules out Verticillium Wilt (gradual, with yellow V-patterns)
- Bacterial Wilt (Ralstonia solanacearum) causes exactly this rapid green wilt from vascular occlusion
- Southern Bacterial Wilt is the same pathogen but the field presentation matches Bacterial_Wilt class description
